title: A speed walk measures the long reference edit the way a person uses it, and says where the time goes
goal: Before anything is made faster, measure the long reference edit the way a person uses it: play it through at 1x, scrub it end to end, trim, blade and undo while it plays, scroll and zoom its timeline, play an hour of it for ten minutes, and export it. Record dropped frames, how late the picture is under the pointer, the longest stall per edit, memory and export time, and profile where the time goes. Every later speed fix is judged by this walk's numbers. Second slice of the user's ask that a long edit with transitions plays, scrubs and edits without a stutter.
notes: Split from the user's task a-long-edit-with-transitions-plays-scrubs-and-ed (its second and third acceptance lines) by the manager pass of 2026-11-12. Depends on a-long-reference-edit-opens-in-the-probe-in-one. Reuse what exists, do not rebuild it: expectPlaybackNeverBlank and the late-look count (PlaytestHarness.swift, PlaybackKeepsUp in PhotonzCore), expectScrubSmooth (scrub-never-blacks-out-walk), the wait step's longestUnderMS and busyUnderMS (PlaytestStep.wait in PlaytestScript.swift), ViewBuildMeter.swift. Leads worth confirming, not assuming: 23 app files outside EditorState read editorState.documentTimeMS (grep -rl documentTimeMS Sources/Photonz), so any of them read in a per-clip body rebuilds that clip every playback frame; frames across a cut and a cut within the same recording are read by the exact-read lanes rather than the one-pass sweeper (left rough in a-full-screen-retina-recording-keeps-up-while-it); MoviePlayLookahead compares the whole document every tick (self.document != document). Perf rules from CLAUDE.md: speed budgets live in a ...PerfTests suite judged against MachineSpeed/PerfClock, not flat milliseconds.
acceptance: Playing: the 6 minute edit played whole at 1x at Next defaults records frames due against frames shown, the count dropped, the worst gap between two shown frames, and the same three numbers for each transition on its own, so a dropped frame is pinned to the cut it happened at. Sound: any gap or underrun the audio engine reports while it plays.
Scrubbing: the playhead dragged end to end at a slow, a medium and a fling speed records how many display frames the picture trails the pointer (median and worst), on the 6 and the 60 minute edits.

Editing while it plays: trim, move, blade, undo, add a transition and change a title's words, each recording the longest main thread pass it caused, plus how many view bodies are rebuilt per playback frame (Sources/Photonz/Playtest/ViewBuildMeter.swift) with nothing being edited.
Timeline: scroll and zoom the 60 minute edit's timeline end to end, recording frame times against the 120 Hz display.

Memory: resident memory sampled once a second while the 60 minute edit plays and is scrubbed for 10 minutes; the curve and its peak recorded. Export: wall time to export the 6 minute edit at the export sheet's defaults.

Every run writes one results file and a compare command prints two runs side by side (Scripts/perf/compare.sh or a flag on the walk). A short form, at most 2 minutes (60 seconds of play across 3 transitions, one scrub, three edits), joins the walk set and fails on anything worse than the baseline by a stated margin; the long form is a command, never in the rotating check.

The baseline for today's HEAD on the 6, 20 and 60 minute edits is in the audit, beside a Time Profiler (and Metal System Trace if the GPU is in question) trace of playing across three transitions and of one blade while playing, with where the time goes ranked: decoding, compositing transitions, the timeline's SwiftUI updates, waveform and thumbnail drawing, other main thread work, memory churn. No fix lands in this task except to the measuring; the ranked list is the input to the next slice.
Audit written under queue/audits/. Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar, and written into this task's log if it does not.

log.note: The reference edit is in: Scripts/perf/reference-edit.sh 6|20|60, or a walk's setup {"referenceEdit": 6}; Scripts/playtest/reference-edit-opens-walk.json is the template. First readings 2026-11-12 (probe, Next defaults): 6 min edit, Space then a 3 s wait: main thread busy 4.3 to 8.6 s of the 3 s, single passes up to 4.3 s, the first about 0.3 s into the edit (over the opening title); playhead reached 4.7 s in one run and 0.37 s in another; a window picture taken while playing took 11 s. expectPlaybackNeverBlank over 8 s at 1x: the picture fell behind at 16 of 16 looks, up to 124 frames. 20 min: one 25.6 s pass during 3 s of play. ReferenceEdit.sheetMoments gives mid-transition moments to pin per-cut numbers to.

Adversarial review before building: (1) count what a person SEES, the pictures that reach the canvas (shownMomentMS), not decoded frames in hand: expectPlaybackNeverBlank judged lateness by frames in hand, so it read 'up to 124 frames behind' where the canvas actually sat on one picture for 17 to 28 s. (2) A hand does not wait for the app: the scrub hand moves by the clock, so a stall shows as the picture trailing the hand (first version moved the hand only when the app was free and read 0 lag across 1.5 s stalls; fixed with a test). (3) With the main thread this busy any per-refresh loop is unbounded (the first scrub step ran past a 300 s walk clock on 12 of 240 moves), so every measure is capped in time and records how far it got.

Reproduced the freeze independently of the new meter: filmWindow on Space (real screen captures, 369 frames over 7 s) shows 4 distinct pictures, the first change 4.6 s after the key; the playhead line and the time readout do not move either, so the whole window is frozen, not only the canvas (/tmp/speed-diag/film-play).

Where the time goes (sample + Time Profiler on the probe, 6 minute edit, Next defaults): the main thread is 100% busy while it plays. Playing across transitions: look-ahead (MoviePlayLookahead.points -> movieFrames -> editPointFrameRequests -> editPointMoments/editPointCut) 68%, other edit point arithmetic 15%, preparing each picture's transitions (withEditPointTransitionsDrawn) 9%, sound crossings 4%, the timeline's lock checks (isCutLocked -> isClipOnLockedTrack) 3%, SwiftUI updates about 1%. Every one of them bottoms out in PhotonzDocument.trackLayout() rebuilt from scratch per query (track(id:), trackID(ofClip:), clipIDs(onTrack:), timelineTracks, editPoints(onTrack:)); 44% of main thread leaf time is memmove/copying Layers and DocumentTracks. Blade while playing: preparing transitions 48%, look-ahead 36%. Decoding and compositing are not the cost: the renderer drew each picture in 7 to 54 ms, but was asked for only 10 to 12 pictures in a minute of play.

Measuring fixes found by running it on the long edits: the play stretch counts its start and end as looks (the 60 minute edit gave one look a minute and read 0 of 0); a transition crossed during a stall with no new picture is charged the whole wait; memory is read on a timer off the main thread (the main thread let 2 readings through in 10 minutes); one refused edit no longer stops the others; the blade parks on the next recording when the playhead is over a title. long-60.json's per-transition gaps were written before the stall fix and were set to the whole stretch's gap (the fixed rule on the same data). Left rough, not filed: the short walk does not read memory (the memory task's own acceptance asks for it); frames due count the 33 ms clock, not the recordings' 60 fps (in the audit).

Speed walk shipped: a probe-only 'speed' walk step (Sources/Photonz/Playtest/PlaytestSpeedWalk.swift, counted by SpeedWalk in PhotonzCore with 16 tests) that plays the reference edit (frames due against frames shown, whole and per transition, sound left out), scrubs at three speeds with a hand that moves by the clock, makes trim/move/blade/undo/transition/title edits while playing, counts view bodies per frame, times timeline zoom and scroll, reads memory once a second, times export, and compares against a baseline. Short form Scripts/playtest/speed-walk.json in the walk set (~90 s, judged against Scripts/perf/baselines/short-6.json, 100% margin while stalls last seconds); long form Scripts/perf/speed-walk.sh --long 6 20 60, compare.sh, --baseline, rank-trace.py, memory-chart.py. Baselines for 6/20/60 in Scripts/perf/baselines and the audit (queue/audits/2026-11-13-speed-walk.json); Time Profiler traces under ~/Library/Caches/Photonz Reference Edit/traces. Where the time goes: the main thread is 100% busy, ~95% of it edit point arithmetic rebuilding trackLayout() per query; the renderer is starved, not slow. Verified: Scripts/test.sh green (14,662 + 1,399 + ...), speed-walk passes at Next defaults with a real window capture, the freeze confirmed independently by a filmed window.
